title: Fourier norm after reindexing a coefficient function
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and let $S\\subseteq J$. For each assignment $z$ of signs outside $J$, take the Fourier coefficient indexed by $S$ of the restriction of $f$ to $J$; this gives a real-valued function of $z$. The Fourier one-norm of this function, with the outside coordinates reindexed by a cube of the same dimension, equals the sum of the absolute values of its Fourier coefficients indexed by subsets of the outside-coordinate set.
hypotheses_covered: $J$ is a finite set of coordinates
